definitions.explanation: An honorific title used to address or refer to an emperor, empress, king, or queen. In Japan, used exclusively for the Emperor and Empress.

examples.japanese: {天皇|てんのう}{陛下|へいか}のお{言葉|ことば}がありました。
examples.english: There were words from His Majesty the Emperor.

examples.japanese: {両|りょう}{陛下|へいか}は{被災地|ひさいち}を{訪問|ほうもん}された。
examples.english: Their Majesties visited the disaster-affected area.

examples.japanese: {国賓|こくひん}として{招|まね}かれた{国王|こくおう}{陛下|へいか}が{空港|くうこう}に{到着|とうちゃく}された。
examples.english: His Majesty the King, invited as a state guest, arrived at the airport.

notes:
The highest honorific title for a monarch. In Japan, applies only to the {天皇|てんのう} (Emperor) and {皇后|こうごう} (Empress).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {天皇|てんのう}{陛下|へいか} (His Majesty the Emperor)
- {皇后|こうごう}{陛下|へいか} (Her Majesty the Empress)
- {両|りょう}{陛下|へいか} (Their Majesties — the Emperor and Empress together)
- {国王|こくおう}{陛下|へいか} (His Majesty the King)
- {女王|じょおう}{陛下|へいか} (Her Majesty the Queen)

The word {陛|へい} originally referred to the steps leading up to the throne. Addressing the emperor through the steps (rather than directly) was considered properly respectful.

Do not confuse with {殿下|でんか} (His/Her Royal Highness), used for princes, princesses, and other members of the imperial family below the emperor.
